answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, with the lock held through a challenge window. If linked accounts coordinate to fake demand or steal payouts, evidence of duplicate control can trigger slashing, so creating a thousand accounts multiplies the attacker’s exposed stake rather than their influence for free. A bridge can make the rule legible across chains; cedar and wander may be harmless account names, but neither avoids the deposit or the risk of losing it.
